diseases.name: Blossom End Rot
diseases.pathogen: Calcium shortage in the growing fruit (uneven watering)
diseases.description: A disorder, not an infection: the end of the fruit away from the stalk dies because too little calcium reaches it while it grows.
diseases.causes: Uneven watering (dry spells then heavy watering), drought, root damage or too much nitrogen keep calcium from reaching the fruit; it is rarely a lack of calcium in the soil.
symptoms: Water-soaked patch at the blossom end of the fruit
The patch turns sunken, tan to black and leathery
Moulds may grow on the dead patch
diseases.effect: Affected fruit is spoiled; later fruit is fine once watering is even.
diseases.untreated: Fruit keeps being lost while watering stays uneven.

steps.title: Remove spoiled fruit
steps.instruction: Pick off affected fruit so the plant feeds the healthy ones.

steps.title: Water evenly
steps.instruction: Keep the soil evenly moist; mulch to hold moisture.
steps.rationale: Even water moves calcium into the fruit.

steps.title: Ease off nitrogen
steps.instruction: Use a balanced feed, not heavy nitrogen.
steps.rationale: Lush leaves draw calcium away from the fruit.

prevention.title: Water regularly, mulch
prevention.detail: Steady moisture is the main prevention.

prevention.title: Test the soil pH and calcium
prevention.detail: Lime only if the test shows a need.

lifecycle: Fruit grows fast in warm weather.
Uneven water slows calcium reaching its far end.
Cells there die: a water-soaked patch appears.
The patch sinks and turns dark and leathery.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: bell pepper blossom end rot

diseases.name: Frogeye Leaf Spot
diseases.description: A fungal leaf spot of pepper with pale-centred, dark-ringed spots.
diseases.causes: Spores survive on infected debris and seed and spread by wind and rain splash in warm, humid weather.
symptoms: Round spots with light grey centres
A dark brown ring round each spot (the 'frog eye')
diseases.effect: Leaf drop exposes fruit to sunscald and reduces yield.

steps.title: Remove spotted leaves
steps.instruction: Pick off spotted leaves when the plants are dry.

steps.title: Protective fungicide
steps.instruction: Spray a registered product following the label.

prevention.title: Rotate crops
prevention.detail: Leave two years before peppers return.

lifecycle: The fungus survives on debris and seed.
Wind and splash carry spores to leaves.
Grey-centred spots with dark rings form.
